device.description: 12-bit low-power single-channel voltage-output DAC (VDD as reference) with 3-wire SPI-compatible interface
device.note: dac7512.pdf (SBAS156B) p.2 pin configurations (SOT23-6, MSOP-8) and pin description, p.3 power requirements (VDD 2.7-5.5 V), p.4 timing characteristics and serial write operation diagram (SYNC falls with SCLK high, data clocked on SCLK falling edges), p.12 serial interface, input shift register (Figure 3), SYNC interrupt (Figure 4), power-on reset (zero), power-down modes (Table I)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: DAC register; power-on reset fills it with zeros (0 V) until a valid write

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: internal: PD1/PD0 (DB13/DB12) of the last valid frame, Table I (00 normal operation)

commands.name: WRITE
commands.note: DB15-DB14 don't care, DB13-DB12 PD1/PD0, DB11-DB0 data; executed on the 16th SCLK falling edge; SYNC high before it aborts the frame (SYNC interrupt)

pages: p.2 (pin configurations, pin description), p.3 (VDD 2.7-5.5 V), p.4 (timing characteristics, serial write operation), p.12 (serial interface, input shift register Figure 3, SYNC interrupt Figure 4, power-on reset, power-down Table I)
notModeled: analog output, resistor string and output amplifier (VOUT never driven)
power-down output loads (1 kOhm / 100 kOhm / Hi-Z): PD1/PD0 are stored in CTRL.PD only
power-up time from power-down (2.5-5 us) and output settling
SCLK frequency (30 MHz / 20 MHz) and setup/hold limits t1-t8
variants: DAC7512E (MSOP-8, DGK) and DAC7512N (SOT23-6, DBV): same die and 16-bit frame; pinouts differ (MSOP has two NC pins). DAC7513 (dac7513.pdf) is the external-reference version with VREF and VFB pins.
